story.title: Lionel Messi Announces Retirement from International Soccer After 21 Years
story.summary: Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international soccer, concluding a remarkable 21-year career with the Argentina national team. The decision follows his participation in six World Cups and scoring 98 international goals, including leading Argentina to the World Cup final in July. Messi shared the news via social media, expressing the emotional weight of his choice.

explore_lenses.label: Why did Messi choose to retire now?
explore_lenses.title: A decision shaped after the World Cup
explore_lenses.summary: Messi said he had been considering retirement since Argentina's World Cup-final loss and felt he had given all he could to the national team. His statement also said younger players deserved their opportunity.

claims.text: Messi said he wrote his retirement message on July 21, 2026—two days after Argentina lost the World Cup final to Spain—and that he had reflected on the decision in the time since.
Messi's stated perspective was that he had 'nothing more to give' and that younger players behind him deserved places with Argentina.
The AFA described the 2026 final as Messi's sixth World Cup and said he led Argentina to the final with eight goals and four assists during the tournament.

The AFA described the 2026 final as Messi's sixth World Cup and said he led Argentina to the final with eight goals and four assists during the tournament.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Messi's public statement gives his reasons, but it does not say whether he considered a farewell match or a future non-playing role with the team.

explore_lenses.label: How did Argentina reach this point?
explore_lenses.title: A final run that extended a trophy era
explore_lenses.summary: Argentina entered the 2026 tournament as defending champions and reached another final through a series of comeback wins, before losing 1-0 to Spain after extra time. The run capped a Messi-Scaloni period that the AFA credits with major titles.

claims.text: Argentina lost the July 19, 2026 World Cup final 1-0 to Spain after extra time; Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute.
FIFA reported that Argentina came from behind to beat England 2-1 in the semifinal, with Lautaro Martínez scoring the 92nd-minute winner; Messi assisted both Argentina goals, according to the AFA.
The AFA's assessment is that Messi and coach Lionel Scaloni led an era including two Copa Américas, the 2022 Finalissima, the 2022 World Cup and the 2026 World Cup final.
Messi finished the 2026 World Cup with a record 34 tournament appearances, according to FIFA.

explore_lenses.label: What changes for Argentina next?
explore_lenses.title: A leadership transition with two open questions
explore_lenses.summary: Messi's retirement removes Argentina's captain and central on-field leader just as the future of coach Lionel Scaloni is also unsettled. Scaloni said after the final that he would remain through December but expected to stop afterward.

claims.text: Scaloni said after the World Cup final that he would continue through December 2026, when his contract ends, but that he likely would not remain as Argentina coach afterward.

The AFA characterized Messi as Argentina's footballing and emotional leader during the 2026 World Cup, so his exit creates a captaincy and leadership succession issue independent of any coaching decision.
Forecast: Argentina may undergo both captain and coach transitions by the end of 2026 if Scaloni follows through on his stated expectation to leave after his contract expires.

story_report.summary: Lionel Messi has ended his 21-year international career with Argentina after scoring 98 goals and appearing in six World Cups. In explaining the decision, Messi said he felt he had nothing more to give and that younger players deserved opportunities. His departure leaves Argentina facing an immediate leadership transition after the AFA characterized him as the team’s footballing and emotional leader during its 2026 World Cup campaign.

sections.heading: Messi’s Decision Followed World Cup Defeat
sections.body: Messi said he wrote his retirement message on July 21, two days after Argentina lost the World Cup final, and reflected on the decision afterward. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time on July 19, with Ferran Torres scoring in the 106th minute. The final was Messi’s sixth World Cup, according to the AFA, which said he led Argentina’s tournament run with eight goals and four assists.

sections.heading: Messi’s Argentina Career Spanned Historic Run
sections.body: Messi completed the 2026 tournament with a record 34 World Cup appearances, FIFA said. Argentina reached the final after a 2-1 semifinal victory over England, in which Lautaro Martínez scored the 92nd-minute winner; the AFA said Messi assisted both Argentine goals. The AFA described the Messi-Scaloni era as including two Copa Américas, the 2022 Finalissima, the 2022 World Cup and the 2026 World Cup final.

sections.heading: Argentina Faces Leadership Transition After Messi
sections.body: Argentina must address captaincy and leadership succession following Messi’s exit, while coach Lionel Scaloni has said he plans to remain through December 2026, when his contract ends, but likely will not continue afterward. If Scaloni leaves as anticipated, Argentina could undergo both captain and coaching transitions by year’s end. The consulted AFA and FIFA materials do not identify successors for either role.

related_stories.title: Ebola Outbreak in DRC Exceeds 6,000 Cases with Nearly 3,000 Deaths
related_stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 6,000 confirmed cases, with the death toll reaching 2,911. This outbreak is noted as the largest in the country's history and one of the fastest-growing Ebola epidemics ever recorded. Over 1,360 individuals have reportedly recovered from the virus.

related_stories.title: Severe Flooding in Nepal and Tibet Leaves Nearly 1,000 Dead and Thousands Missing
related_stories.summary: Severe flooding along the Nepal-China border has resulted in nearly 1,000 confirmed deaths, with over 4,000 individuals reported missing. The disaster has caused significant despair among families affected by the floods. Relief efforts are being severely hampered by heavy rain, which has turned roads into mud, complicating rescue operations.
